We note that while many of the meth- ods above improve the memory to arithmetic-operations ratio, in cases where the ratio remains high, these methods and our speculative decoding method might be effective in tandem. Two prior methods leverage speculative execution for speed- ing up decoding from autoregressive models. Blockwise Parallel Decoding (Stern et al., 2018) decodes several to- kens in parallel, similarly to our work. However, it only supports greedy decoding (temperature=0) and not the gen- eral stochastic setting, it requires additional training of a custom model, and focuses on preserving down-stream task quality, instead of guaranteeing identical outputs. Shallow Aggressive Decoding (SAD) (Sun et al., 2021) also decodes several tokens in parallel, similarly to our work. Unlike our work, SAD only supports copying the input to the out- 7Fast Inference from Transformers via Speculative Decoding put, and not general approximation models, making it only suitable for the cases where the inputs and outputs are very similar like grammatical error correction. In addition, simi- larly to Blockwise Parallel Decoding, SAD does not support the general stochastic sampling setting. After we initially published our work, an independent im- plementation of speculative decoding (Chen et al., 2023) showed similar 2X-2.5X improvements on Chinchilla 70B. 6. Discussion We presented speculative sampling which enables efﬁcient stochastic speculative execution - i.e. speculative execu- tion in the stochastic setting. We analyzed its impact on decoding from autoregressive models like Transformers via speculative decoding and have shown that given enough compute resources, we get meaningful 2X-3X speedups in practice vs T5X, a popular optimized implementation. One limitation of speculative execution in general, and of speculative decoding in particular, is that latency is im- proved through increased concurrency at the cost of an in- creased number of arithmetic operations. Thus, our method is not helpful for conﬁgurations where additional compu- tation resources are not available. However, in common cases where additional computation resources are available (e.g. when memory bandwidth is the bottleneck) our method provides the speedup with signiﬁcant beneﬁts: the model architecture doesn’t change, retraining isn’t required, and most importantly, the output distribution is guaranteed to stay the same. Our method is easy to implement, and can be used to speedup inference using out-of-the-box models without developing and evaluating custom schemes. There are several directions for follow up research, impor- tantly, further investigating the compatibility of speculative decoding with beam search (see Appendix A.4). Also, while our method yields substantial speedups with existing off-the- shelf approximation models, greater improvements might be obtained via custom approximation models (Section 3.6), such as those with custom architectures (e.g. custom sizes, non-autoregressive models, or various heuristics) or with custom training procedures (e.g. standard distillation with soft targets from Mp, or optimizing Mq for αdirectly). It could also be interesting to explore a hierarchical version of the algorithm, where the approximation model is itself accelerated by an even faster model, which could allow for more capable approximation models. In this work we ﬁxed the approximation model and the number of guesses γthroughout inference, but varying them during inference could yield additional improvements (Section 3.5). In our 6Note that the outputs from the LaMDA model always go through a Top40 ﬁlter. This has no effect on argmax, but does have some effect on standard sampling. experiments we always performed the same standardization on the distributions generated by the approximation model as the desired one for the target model (Section 2.2), but fur- ther improvements might be obtained by applying different transformations. We tested speculative decoding only in the text modality, but it might work well in other domains (e.g. images) which would be interesting to experiment with. Finally, we note that stochastic speculative execution and speculative sampling can be helpful outside the scope of speculative decoding from autoregressive models. For ex- ample, given two slow functions, f(x) and g(y) such that f(x) generates a distribution from which g’s input is sam- pled, we could use our method to run f and g in parallel. This setup might arise e.g. in physics simulations, or in rein- forcement learning where f is a large model that produces a distribution on actions, and gis the world simulation, which would be interesting to explore. llm_extracted_info.main_contributions: The paper introduces 'speculative decoding', a novel algorithm to accelerate inference from large autoregressive models like Transformers without changing the model architecture, retraining, or altering the output distribution. The core contributions are: (1) Generalizing speculative execution to stochastic settings through a new method called 'speculative sampling'. (2) A practical decoding mechanism that uses a smaller, faster approximation model to generate candidate tokens in advance, which are then validated in parallel by the large target model, enabling the generation of multiple tokens per single serial run of the target model. The method achieves a 2X-3X wall-time speedup on T5-XXL.
llm_extracted_info.methodology: The methodology, named speculative decoding, uses an efficient approximation model (Mq) to autoregressively generate a short sequence of γ candidate tokens. The slower, large target model (Mp) then processes the entire sequence of candidates in a single parallel forward pass to get their respective probability distributions. A novel sampling technique, 'speculative sampling', is used to accept a prefix of these candidates by comparing the probabilities from Mq and Mp. This process guarantees that the final output distribution is identical to sampling from Mp alone. For each parallel run of Mp, the algorithm generates at least one token and potentially up to γ+1 tokens.
llm_extracted_info.experimental_setup: The method was evaluated on several models and tasks. For wall-time measurements, a T5-XXL (11B parameters) model was used as the target model (Mp), with smaller off-the-shelf models like T5-small (77M), T5-base (250M), and T5-large (800M) as approximation models (Mq). The tasks included English-to-German translation on WMT EnDe and text summarization on CNN/DM, tested with both argmax (temp=0) and standard (temp=1) sampling. Experiments were run on a single TPU-v4 with a batch size of 1. Additional experiments measured the acceptance rate (α) for a 97M parameter GPT-like model on lm1b and a 137B parameter LaMDA model on a dialog task.
llm_extracted_info.limitations: The primary limitation is that speculative decoding improves latency by increasing concurrency, which in turn increases the total number of arithmetic operations. The method is therefore only effective in scenarios where additional compute resources are available and the system is not compute-bound (e.g., when memory bandwidth is the bottleneck). The paper also notes that a detailed analysis of applying the method to beam search is complex and left for future work.
llm_extracted_info.future_research_directions: The paper suggests several future research directions, including: (1) A more thorough investigation of applying speculative decoding to beam search. (2) Designing custom approximation models (e.g., non-autoregressive, different architectures, or heuristics) or custom training procedures (like distillation or directly optimizing for the acceptance rate α) for better performance. (3) Exploring a hierarchical version where the approximation model is also accelerated. (4) Dynamically varying the number of speculative tokens (γ) during inference. (5) Applying the method to other modalities like images. (6) Using the core speculative sampling idea in other domains like reinforcement learning or physics simulations.

new_method.method:
Motivation:
- Practical gap: In real serving, speculative decoding’s speedups vanish whenever acceptance rate α falls (high temperature/top-p, repetition/ban penalties, long/branchy drafts, or Mq drift). Operators increasingly ask for α SLAs to stabilize tail latency across heterogeneous decode configs, but current methods lack: (i) a cheap, calibrated predictor of acceptability before full Mp verification, (ii) a mechanism to prune unpromising branches without altering Mp’s distribution, and (iii) a closed-loop controller that adapts draft shape to maintain α under bandwidth/KV-cache constraints.
- Why now: (1) Bandwidth-bound kernels and KV reuse dominate on consumer GPUs and offloaded servers; (2) Serving telemetry already logs accept/reject traces, enabling supervised acceptance prediction and online calibration; (3) Micro-models (<10M) fit alongside Mq with prefix/KV caching; (4) Candidate-only logits via selected-column W_out and packed prefix attention are practical; (5) Demand for α SLAs and predictable tail latency is rising.

Methodology:
We propose CAVES: Constrained, Acceptance-aware, Verifier-Efficient Speculation. CAVES preserves Mp’s exact distribution while maximizing tokens-per-Mp-call, via three orthogonal additions to any speculative stack.

1) Acceptance- and reward-aware drafting (distribution-preserving)
- Acceptance estimator aφ: Predicts either α_t(x) = Pr[accept x | ctx] or Δ_t(x) = log pMp(x) − log pMq(x) for top-k candidates per node.
  • Training data: production speculative logs with ground-truth accept/reject, Δ; cover temperatures 0.6–1.2, top-p, penalties, domains.
  • Features: Mq hidden state for last token, candidate embeddings, q-entropy/top-2 margin, repetition/ban signals, decode-config embedding, short α history, distance-to-eos.
  • Objective and calibration: Asymmetric loss to penalize overestimation; temperature scaling + isotonic regression; split-conformal quantile regression to produce conservative lower bounds aφ_LB with coverage ≥ 1−δ. Optional ratio-matching auxiliary loss (e.g., uLSIF/KLIEP) to stabilize Δ estimation.
  • Robustness: Train over randomized Mq temperatures/top-p and use domain/task embeddings to reduce covariate shift.
- Tiny reward scorer rψ: A distilled <10M per-token scorer that ranks candidates given the prefix. Used only to prioritize proposals; acceptance and final sampling still use Mp exactly.
- Draft-tree builder (GPU SSSP/beam hybrid): Build a depth-γ, branching-B tree. Score an edge token x with S = −log q(x) + λR·rψ(x) − λA·max(0, α* − aφ_LB(x)). Selection objective S′ ∝ aφ_LB(x) · exp(rψ/τ) · q(x), with uncertainty gating: downweight aφ when its conformal interval is wide. Non-myopic selection approximates expected accepted-prefix length along a path via ∏j aφ_LB(xj) under a node budget. Online draft temperature adjusts Mq only to nudge q→p when predicted α dips; Mp’s final distribution remains unchanged.
- Implementation: aφ and rψ share a small encoder with prefix/KV caching; a single CUDA/Triton kernel computes candidate features and invokes both micro-models batched over frontier nodes.

2) Cascaded block verification with KV reuse (exactness-preserving)
- Stage A: Cheap partial Mp. Run first L′ layers (quantized) of Mp for all frontier nodes; compute candidate-only logits via selected-column projection W_out[:, C] where C is the union of proposed tokens. Early-exit heads trained on frozen L′ features estimate final logit margins; prune branches using calibrated margin thresholds combined with aφ_LB. Only what goes to Stage B is pruned; final acceptance still uses standard speculative sampling, keeping exactness.
- KV reuse + packing: Reuse Stage-A Mp KVs in Stage B for survivors. Use packed batched prefix attention over many short nodes to increase arithmetic intensity and reduce recompute. For MoE, gate and execute only experts hit by C in Stage A; carry expert masks into Stage B.
- Stage B: Complete layers L′+1..L for survivors; run vanilla acceptance tests and, on rejection, sample from adjusted Mp as in the original algorithm.
- Kernels: Fused gather–matmul for W_out selected columns, persistent kernels to amortize launches, overlap Mq drafting, Stage A, and Stage B on separate streams.

3) α-rate–constrained controller (dual control with safety)
- Objective: Maximize tokens-per-Mp-call subject to α ≥ α* per request.
- Dual update: λA ← clip(λA + η(α* − EMA(αobs)), [0, λmax]). Actuators: depth γ, branching B, Mq temperature, Stage-A prune thresholds. Expand when aφ_LB and bandwidth permit; shrink with α dips or high uncertainty.
- Safety: Conformal intervals act as a “confidence brake” that caps tree expansion in high-variance contexts. Persistent SLA violations trigger fallback to standard speculative decoding.
- Tuning: Choose η via line search on historical traces; assume local Lipschitzness of α in actuators. Controller runs per-request to stabilize tail latency under mixed workloads.

4) Training/data/ops
- aφ: Train offline on instrumented logs; recalibrate online with a small sliding buffer and periodic split-conformal refits to maintain lower-bound coverage. Ablate α vs Δ targets.
- rψ: Distill from an external RM or preference data; optionally share encoder with aφ.
- Footprint: Both micro-models <10M params; Stage A quantized; candidate-only logits minimize bandwidth. All micro-model inference stays on GPU to avoid CPU stalls.
- Integration: Prototype in vLLM or TensorRT-LLM; provide kernels for selected-column W_out, packed prefix attention, and KV reuse across branches.

5) Analysis and guarantees
- Exactness: Unchanged—Stage B uses standard speculative sampling with Mp; Stage A only prunes the set of nodes proceeding to full verification.
- Throughput model: E[tokens per Mp call] ≈ 1 + E[max accepted-prefix length], approximated by ∑paths ∏j aφ_LB(xj) under a node budget; S′ implements a regression-based proxy under bandwidth limits.
- SLA guarantee: If aφ_LB has one-sided coverage ≥ 1−δ and η is below a stability limit, then α violations occur with probability ≤ δ at steady state; uncertainty gating further reduces transient violations.

How CAVES differs from prior work
- Speculative decoding (base algorithm): Adds calibrated acceptance prediction, α-constrained control, and cascaded partial-Mp verification with KV reuse and candidate-only logits—none appear in the original method.
- SpecExec: Retains tree-building but introduces acceptance- and reward-aware scoring, uncertainty-aware pruning, and a cascaded verifier to prevent α collapse in high-entropy regimes; also adds α-SLA control. SpecExec neither predicts acceptability nor constrains α.
- ARGS: Adjusts sampling and changes the distribution. CAVES uses reward only to prioritize proposals and preserves Mp’s exact distribution by verifying with standard acceptance.
- ICO/order statistics: Translates rate-constrained optimization and expected-maximum subset selection into a practical drafting rule with conservative bounds and a decode-time controller for SLAs.

Evaluation plan (concise)
- Models: Llama-2/3 7B–70B, Mixtral-8x7B; consumer GPUs (3090/4090) and A100/PCIe offloading.
- Regimes: temps 0.6–1.2, top-p 0.8–1.0, repetition/ban penalties, long-context, batch 1–8, MoE on/off.
- Metrics: α (P50/P95), tokens/sec, Mp-calls/token, accepted-prefix length, wall-time, GPU util/bandwidth, SLA violation rate, memory traffic, calibration coverage of aφ_LB.
- Ablations: no aφ; no Stage A; no controller; no selected-column logits; Δ vs α targets; L′ depth; micro-model size; uncertainty gating on/off.

Expected impact:
- Stable speedups in difficult regimes: Maintain α ≥ 0.8 with heavy penalties/high entropy while enabling deeper/wider drafts; expect 1.3–2.5× additional speedup over baseline speculative decoding at fixed α, with larger gains on bandwidth-bound/offloaded stacks.
- Predictable serving behavior: First decode-time controller to enforce α SLAs, cutting tail-latency variance across mixed decode configs.
- Drop-in deployability: No Mp retraining; micro-models are tiny, cache-friendly, trained from logs; kernels benefit MoE and consumer GPUs.
- Hardware–software co-design: Candidate-only logits, early-exit heads on partial Mp, and packed prefix attention are reusable primitives for memory-bound accelerators.
- Research avenues: Theory and practice of conservative acceptance prediction, uncertainty-aware subset selection for expected accepted-prefix maximization, and stability of rate-constrained decoding control under resource limits.

experimental_design.experiment_strategy:
Experiment 1 — Acceptance estimator aφ: calibration, coverage, and drafting gains
Purpose
- Show that a tiny acceptance estimator with conformal calibration delivers reliable lower bounds aφ_LB that (i) meet one-sided coverage and (ii) translate into better draft construction and more tokens-per-Mp-call at equal or lower α violation rate.

Setup
- Models: Mp = Llama-3-8B (HF transformers, float16), Mq = Mistral-7B or Llama-3-8B-instruct distilled to 3–7B; both loaded with device_map="auto". Optionally quantize Mq to int8.
- Data: 20K prompts sampled from: OpenOrca/ShareGPT style chat logs + Wiki passages (mix instruction and continuation). Decode regimes randomly assigned per prompt: temperature ∈ {0.6, 0.8, 1.0, 1.2}, top-p ∈ {0.8, 0.9, 0.95, 1.0}, repetition penalty ∈ {1.0, 1.1, 1.2}, ban-lists ∈ {none, 5 common repeats}, max new tokens 128.
- Hardware: single 24–48 GB GPU (3090/4090/A6000). Seed torch and numpy for reproducibility.

Data collection (baseline speculative decoding)
- Implement standard tree speculative decoding with Mq proposals and Mp verification (depth γ∈{3,4}, branching B∈{2,4}). For each frontier node candidate token x:
  - Log features: last-token hidden hq (dim d) from Mq, candidate token embedding e(x), q(x) logprob, top-2 margin, local entropy Hq, repetition/ban flags, decode-config embedding (one-hot), short α history (last 4 accepts), distance-to-eos.
  - Labels: accept ∈ {0,1}, Δ = log pMp(x) − log pMq(x), and α_t context-wise accept rate over node’s siblings.
  - Save also the full context length at node, and whether token was on the accepted path.
- Schema: a list of dicts or a Parquet dataset; ensure per-candidate rows with prompt_id, step_id, node_id.
- Collect 1–2M candidate rows in ~2–3 hours on a single GPU (γ×B≈8 candidates/step × ~100 steps × 20K prompts).

Model aφ and training
- Architecture: Tiny MLP (<5M params), inputs: [LayerNorm(hq); e(x); q_logprob; top2_margin; Hq; rep_flag; decode_cfg_embed; α_hist; dist_eos]. Two heads:
  - Head α: sigmoid outputs p̂(accept | ctx, x).
  - Head Δ: scalar regression for Δ.
- Loss: L = BCE(accept, p̂; pos_weight=2.0) + 0.1·Huber(Δ, Δ̂). Class-imbalance handled by pos_weight.
- Optimizer: AdamW(lr=2e-4, wd=0.01), batch 32K candidates, 2–3 epochs.
- Calibration: temperature-scaling on α-head logits (optimize NLL on val). Then isotonic regression (sklearn) on the scaled probabilities. Split-conformal quantile for one-sided lower bound:
  - Split validation into calib set C; compute residuals r_i = p̂_iso(i) − 1{accept_i}.
  - qδ = quantile_{1−δ} of r over C.
  - Define aφ_LB = clip(p̂_iso − qδ, 0, 1). Use δ=0.05 by default.

Evaluation A: calibration and generalization
- Protocol: Hold out prompts with unseen decode configs (e.g., only evaluate on T=1.2, top-p=0.9 if not seen together in train). Compute:
  - Coverage: Pr[ accept=1 | aφ_LB ≥ t ] for t-grid; and one-sided coverage Pr[accept ≤ aφ_LB + ε] ≥ 1−δ at ε≈0.
  - AUC/APS for α-head; MAE for Δ-head.
  - Overestimation penalty: E[max(0, aφ − accept)].
- Baselines: heuristics (q_logprob only), margin-only, uncalibrated α-head.
- Success: one-sided coverage ≥ 0.95 across regimes; AUC ≥ 0.80; overestimation reduced by ≥30% vs heuristics.

Evaluation B: offline drafting effectiveness
- Offline shadow simulation: For each prompt and step, use Mq to propose up to γ×B candidates. Rank candidates using S′ ∝ aφ_LB · exp(rψ/τ) · q(x). For this experiment set rψ≡0 (ablation later).
- Under a node budget N=γ×B, build the path with max product ∏j aφ_LB(xj) and simulate actual acceptance by calling Mp to verify in the loop. Record accepted-prefix length and α.
- Compare against: (i) uniform beam over q(x); (ii) top-q(x) only; (iii) Δ̂-only ranking.
- Metrics: E[accepted-prefix length], Mp-calls/token, α mean/P95, and “LB-miss” rate (accept=1 but aφ_LB<α*).
- Success: +15–30% accepted-prefix length at fixed α; ≥2× reduction in LB-miss vs uncalibrated.

Ablations
- With/without Δ-head; with/without decode-config embedding; train at a single temperature vs mixed.
- rψ: add a tiny 2-layer MLP trained on next-token logprob under Mp as proxy reward; show S′ improves accepted-prefix length a few percent without hurting α.

Implementation sketch (PyTorch)
- Build dataset: tensors for features and labels; DDP not required.
- Train aφ; fit temperature and isotonic; compute qδ.
- Drafting sim: vectorize candidate scoring over batches; evaluate Mp acceptance in a loop for ground truth.

Expected outcome
- Demonstrates (i) reliable conservative acceptance prediction and (ii) that acceptance-aware drafting increases tokens-per-Mp-call without increasing violation rate, validating component (1) of CAVES.


Experiment 2 — Cascaded block verification with candidate-only logits and early-exit margin head
Purpose
- Show that running a cheap partial Mp (Stage A) with selected-column logits and an early-exit head prunes unpromising branches, reducing full Mp compute while preserving exactness and α.

Setup
- Same Mp as Exp1. Choose L′ (e.g., 8 of 32 transformer blocks for 8B model).
- Implement a partial forward that returns the hidden state after L′ and past_key_values for layers 0..L′.

Training the early-exit margin head
- Data: Using 5K prompts, for each context compute final Mp logits at next token; record margin m* = logit(y*) − max_{y≠y*} logit(y). Also record h_{L′} (hidden after L′).
- Train a small MLP gθ(h_{L′}) to predict m*. Loss: Huber. Calibrate a threshold θ_prune via ROC to achieve 99% recall of positives (large margin), so pruning is conservative.

Decode-time pipeline
- For each frontier node:
  1) Stage A: Run Mp layers 0..L′ on the node with cached KVs (reuse across siblings if same prefix). Compute:
     - Candidate-only logits: gather LM head columns W_out[:, C] where C is the union of candidate tokens across the frontier; compute h_{L′}·W_out[:, C].
     - gθ(h_{L′}) per node to get margin estimate; combine with aφ_LB to compute a prune score.
  2) Prune: Drop node-token pairs with [gθ margin < θ_prune] OR [aφ_LB < α*] OR both; ensure that at least one child per node survives to avoid dead-ends.
  3) Stage B: For the survivors, run Mp layers L′+1..L to get final logits and perform standard speculative acceptance. On rejection, sample from Mp as in baseline (ensures exactness).

Controls and baselines
- Baseline-0: vanilla speculative decoding (no Stage A).
- Baseline-1: Stage A but no pruning (measure overhead alone).
- Baseline-2: Full logits (no selected-column gather) to quantify bandwidth savings.

Metrics
- End-to-end tokens/sec; Mp flops/token proxy = (n_full·L + n_partial·L′)/tokens.
- Fraction of branches pruned; precision/recall of pruning vs final acceptance (should be high recall for rejects).
- α mean/P95; output equivalence: with fixed RNG seeds, run 1K prompts and compare exact text outputs vs Baseline-0 (expect near-identical; any discrepancy indicates a bug violating exactness).
- GPU time: measure Stage A and Stage B ms/token with torch.cuda.Event timing; memory traffic proxy via CUDA profiler (optional).

Implementation details (HF Transformers)
- Partial forward: rewrap model to iterate blocks; stop at L′; return h_{L′}. Retain past_key_values for layers 0..L′ in a dict; resume from L′ for survivors by passing remaining KVs (or recompute 0..L′ for survivors if reuse is hard; even without KV reuse, pruning benefit should show at moderate B,γ).
- Candidate-only logits: W_sel = W_out[:, C]; logits_C = h_{L′} @ W_sel; use torch.index_select for gather.
- Batch branches by length using pad/pack to keep kernels efficient.

Success criteria
- ≥15% reduction in full-layer tokens processed (Stage B) with identical α relative to Baseline-0.
- ≥10% wall-clock speedup at γ∈{3,4}, B∈{2,4} vs Baseline-0 on a 4090.
- Output equality ≥99% of runs with fixed seeds, confirming exactness preservation.


Experiment 3 — α-SLA constrained controller under mixed decode configs
Purpose
- Demonstrate that the dual controller maintains α ≥ α* with low violation rate and improves tokens/sec vs static settings across heterogeneous temperatures/top-p/penalties.

Setup
- Use aφ_LB from Exp1; Stage A optional (on for best results). Define α* ∈ {0.7, 0.8, 0.9}. Use mixed workload: per request, sample a decode-config from the Exp1 regime distribution.
- Controller state per request: λA initialized to 0, EMA for αobs with β=0.9.
- Actuators: γ ∈ [2,6], B ∈ [1,6], Mq temperature Tq ∈ [0.7,1.0]. Optionally a Stage-A prune threshold scale.
- Update: after each verify step, observe αobs (accept or reject for each proposed token), update EMA and λA ← clip(λA + η(α* − EMA), [0, λmax]). Choose η in {0.05, 0.1}.
- Draft selection uses S′ ∝ aφ_LB · q(x) with penalty term −λA·max(0, α* − aφ_LB). Expand/shrink tree by allocating node budget N based on λA and uncertainty (wider conformal intervals ⇒ smaller N).

Protocol
- Run 3K requests of 128 tokens target length. Compare:
  - Static: fixed γ=3, B=2, Tq=0.9, no α control.
  - Heuristic: increase Tq when α drops (no aφ), clamp γ,B.
  - CAVES controller: full scheme above.
- For reproducibility, fix seeds per request; randomize decode configs identically across arms.

Metrics
- α P50/P95 and SLA violation rate = Pr[α_window < α*] using rolling windows of 16 proposals; report per-request and global.
- Tokens/sec (median, P95 tail), Mp-calls/token, accepted-prefix length.
- Controller stability: variance of λA, frequency of fallback to baseline speculative.
- Overhead: % time in aφ and control logic.

Implementation sketch (Python)
- Controller loop per request:
  - While not done:
    1) Build candidate set with current γ,B,Tq using Mq; score with aφ_LB and S′.
    2) Optionally run Stage A prune.
    3) Run standard Mp acceptance for the surviving path; log accept/rejects.
    4) Update EMA and λA; adjust actuators for next step.
- Use torch.cuda.Event to time; log to JSONL.

Success criteria
- SLA: violation rate ≤ δ=0.05 at α* target; P95 α ≥ α* − 0.02.
- Throughput: ≥10–25% tokens/sec improvement vs Static at same α*; ≥2× reduction in P95 tail-latency tokens/sec variability.
- Overhead: controller + aφ < 8% of wall time.


Cross-experiment notes
- Exactness checks: ensure final acceptance uses Mp identically to baseline; no sampling from Mq in the final output; any pruning only affects which branches get verified, not the acceptance rule.
- Reproducibility: torch.set_deterministic(True); set cudnn flags accordingly; use fixed seeds for both Mp and Mq RNG.
- Feasibility: All components are implementable in pure Python + PyTorch; optional CUDA kernels (selected-column matmul) provide extra speed but are not required to demonstrate effectiveness.
- Deliverables: scripts for (i) data logging, (ii) aφ training + calibration, (iii) early-exit head training, (iv) decode runners for the three arms, and (v) analysis notebooks that produce coverage plots, speedups, and α SLA charts.
experimental_design.experiment_details:
Overview
This specification details three integrated experiments that validate and stress-test CAVES: (1) training and calibrating a tiny acceptance estimator aφ and demonstrating drafting gains; (2) cascaded partial-Mp verification with candidate-only logits and an early-exit margin head to prune branches without affecting exactness; (3) an α-SLA controller that stabilizes acceptance rates across heterogeneous decode configs while improving throughput. All experiments assume Hugging Face Transformers and PyTorch; quantization and calibration use off-the-shelf libraries.

Environment and dependencies
- Python 3.10+
- PyTorch 2.2+ (CUDA 11.8+), torchvision (optional), torch.compile optional
- transformers 4.41+
- accelerate 0.30+, bitsandbytes 0.43+ (optional, for 8-bit Mq or Stage A)
- scikit-learn 1.4+ (isotonic regression, metrics), scipy 1.11+
- numpy, pandas, pyarrow, tqdm, rich (logging)
- Optional profiling: torch-tb-profiler or Nsight Systems

Global settings
- Set deterministic behavior where possible: torch.manual_seed(1337), numpy.random.seed(1337), torch.backends.cudnn.deterministic=True, torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True). Note: Some fused kernels may still introduce nondeterminism; for exactness tests, also fix sampling seeds and disable kernel autotune.
- Mixed precision: fp16/bf16 for Mp and Mq (bf16 if supported), full fp32 for calibration and tiny heads.
- Device: single 24–48 GB GPU (e.g., 3090/4090/A6000). If needed, offload Mq to int8 with bitsandbytes.

Shared dataset and logging for Experiments 1–3
- Prompts: 20K from mixed instruction/QA (OpenOrca/ShareGPT) + 20K wiki-like continuations (if capacity permits); default 20K total as per strategy. Tokenizer and special tokens consistent with Mp and Mq.
- Decode configs sampled per prompt: temperature ∈ {0.6, 0.8, 1.0, 1.2}, top-p ∈ {0.8, 0.9, 0.95, 1.0}, repetition penalty ∈ {1.0, 1.1, 1.2}, ban list ∈ {none, common 5 repeats}, max_new_tokens=128.
- Baseline speculative decoding to log per-candidate features and labels. Use branching B ∈ {2,4}, depth γ ∈ {3,4}. Collect 1–2M candidate rows.
- Storage: Write to Parquet, partitioned by split and model config; fields include prompt_id, step_id, node_id, token_id, accept label, Δ, features, decode-config one-hot, context length, accepted_path flag.

Code snippet: baseline speculative logging (simplified)
Note: This is a minimal, readable sketch; production code should pipeline GPU work and batch nodes. This uses a conservative acceptance test where a proposal is accepted if Mp’s sampled token equals the proposed token under identical decode config.

class SpecLogger:
    def __init__(self, mp_name, mq_name, device='cuda', load_in_8bit_mq=True):
        from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer
        self.mp_tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(mp_name, use_fast=True)
        self.mq_tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(mq_name, use_fast=True)
        self.mp = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(mp_name, torch_dtype=torch.float16).to(device).eval()
        self.mq = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(
            mq_name,
            torch_dtype=torch.float16,
            load_in_8bit=load_in_8bit_mq,
            device_map='auto')
        self.device = device
        self.emb_q = self.mq.get_input_embeddings()  # for candidate embeddings
        self.Wp = self.mp.lm_head.weight  # [vocab, hidden]

    @torch.no_grad()
    def _sample_next(self, logits, temperature=1.0, top_p=1.0):
        import torch
        logits = logits / max(temperature, 1e-6)
        if top_p < 1.0:
            sorted_logits, sorted_idx = torch.sort(logits, descending=True)
            probs = torch.softmax(sorted_logits, dim=-1)
            cumprobs = torch.cumsum(probs, dim=-1)
            mask = cumprobs > top_p
            mask[..., 0] = False
            sorted_logits[mask] = -float('inf')
            logits = torch.gather(sorted_logits, -1, torch.argsort(sorted_idx, descending=False))
        probs = torch.softmax(logits, dim=-1)
        return torch.multinomial(probs, num_samples=1).squeeze(-1)

    @torch.no_grad()
    def collect(self, prompts, gamma=3, B=2, cfg_sampler=None, out_parquet='caves_candidates.parquet'):
        import pyarrow as pa, pyarrow.parquet as pq
        import pandas as pd
        rows = []
        pid = 0
        for prompt in prompts:
            cfg = cfg_sampler()
            T, P, rep_pen, bans = cfg['temperature'], cfg['top_p'], cfg['rep_pen'], cfg['bans']
            mp_ids = self.mp_tok(prompt, return_tensors='pt').to(self.device)
            mq_ids = self.mq_tok(prompt, return_tensors='pt').to(self.device)
            # KV caches omitted for brevity; do simple step-by-step
            accepted_hist = []
            step_id = 0
            generated = []
            while step_id < 128:
                # 1) Propose draft tree from Mq of depth gamma and branching B
                frontier = [(mq_ids['input_ids'], [])]  # (ids, tokens_path)
                proposals = []
                for depth in range(gamma):
                    new_frontier = []
                    for ids, path in frontier:
                        out = self.mq(input_ids=ids, use_cache=False)
                        logits_q = out.logits[:, -1, :].float()
                        # Select top-B candidates under q
                        q_probs = torch.softmax(logits_q / max(T, 1e-6), dim=-1)
                        topk = torch.topk(q_probs, k=B)
                        for k in range(B):
                            tok = topk.indices[0, k]
                            qlp = torch.log(q_probs[0, tok])
                            # Features from Mq
                            hq = out.hidden_states[-1][:, -1, :].float() if getattr(out, 'hidden_states', None) is not None else None
                            if hq is None:
                                # re-run with output_hidden_states
                                out = self.mq(input_ids=ids, output_hidden_states=True)
                                hq = out.hidden_states[-1][:, -1, :].float()
                            # additional features
                            sorted_lp, _ = torch.sort(torch.log_softmax(logits_q, dim=-1), descending=True)
                            top2_margin = (sorted_lp[0, 0] - sorted_lp[0, 1]).item()
                            Hq = -(q_probs * torch.log(q_probs + 1e-9)).sum().item()
                            emb_x = self.emb_q(tok).detach().float().cpu().numpy()
                            proposals.append({
                                'prompt_id': pid, 'step_id': step_id,
                                'node_len': ids.shape[-1],
                                'tok': int(tok), 'q_logprob': float(qlp.cpu()),
                                'top2_margin': float(top2_margin),
                                'Hq': float(Hq), 'hq': hq[0].cpu().numpy(),
                                'emb_x': emb_x,
                                'decode_cfg': cfg,
                            })
                            new_ids = torch.cat([ids, tok.view(1, 1).to(ids.device)], dim=-1)
                            new_frontier.append((new_ids, path + [int(tok)])).
                    frontier = new_frontier
                # 2) Verify leading path only (baseline speculative would tree-verify; for logging, verify each candidate cheaply)
                # For labels, compute Mp acceptance and Δ for each candidate using the same prefix.
                outp = self.mp(input_ids=mp_ids['input_ids'])
                p_logits = outp.logits[:, -1, :].float()
                p_lp = torch.log_softmax(p_logits / max(T, 1e-6), dim=-1)
                q_logits = self.mq(input_ids=mq_ids['input_ids']).logits[:, -1, :].float()
                q_lp = torch.log_softmax(q_logits / max(T, 1e-6), dim=-1)
                for row in proposals:
                    tok = row['tok']
                    delta = float((p_lp[0, tok] - q_lp[0, tok]).cpu())
                    # Acceptance indicator: Mp sampled token equals tok under same sampler
                    sampled_tok = int(self._sample_next(p_logits[0], temperature=T, top_p=P).item())
                    accept = 1 if sampled_tok == tok else 0
                    row.update({'delta': delta, 'accept': accept})
                    rows.append(row)
                # Step forward by actually sampling from Mp to keep prompt realistic
                next_tok = self._sample_next(p_logits[0], temperature=T, top_p=P).view(1, 1)
                mp_ids['input_ids'] = torch.cat([mp_ids['input_ids'], next_tok.to(self.device)], dim=-1)
                mq_ids['input_ids'] = torch.cat([mq_ids['input_ids'], next_tok.to(self.device)], dim=-1)
                generated.append(int(next_tok))
                step_id += 1
                if step_id >= 128: break
            pid += 1
        # Write rows to parquet
        import pandas as pd
        df = pd.DataFrame(rows)
        table = pa.Table.from_pandas(df)
        pq.write_table(table, out_parquet)


Experiment 1 — Acceptance estimator aφ: calibration, coverage, and drafting gains
Purpose
- Validate that a tiny acceptance estimator produces conservative lower bounds aφ_LB with guaranteed one-sided coverage and materially improves draft construction, increasing accepted-prefix length and tokens-per-Mp-call at equal or lower α violation rate.

Design
- Train a two-head MLP (<5M params) to predict acceptance probability and Δ; perform post-hoc calibration (temperature scaling + isotonic regression). Build conformal lower bounds via split-conformal quantiles. Evaluate calibration and drafting impact in an offline shadow simulation that calls Mp for ground-truth acceptance along drafted paths.

Feature schema per candidate
- hq: last-token hidden state from Mq, LayerNorm applied at input.
- emb_x: candidate token embedding from Mq’s input embedding.
- q_logprob: log q(x) under Mq with the current decode config.
- top2_margin, Hq: top-2 logit margin and entropy from Mq.
- repetition/ban flags: e.g., whether token repeats last n tokens or in ban list.
- decode-config embedding: one-hot for temperature, top-p, repetition penalty, ban-list bucket.
- α history: last-k accept indicators (k=4) on this request.
- distance_to_eos: tokens since BOS and to max length.

Model architecture and training code

class AlphaEstimator(torch.nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, d_hq, d_emb, d_cfg=16, hidden=1024):
        super().__init__()
        self.ln_hq = torch.nn.LayerNorm(d_hq)
        self.ln_emb = torch.nn.LayerNorm(d_emb)
        self.fc = torch.nn.Sequential(
            torch.nn.Linear(d_hq + d_emb + d_cfg + 6, hidden),
            torch.nn.ReLU(),
            torch.nn.Dropout(0.1),
            torch.nn.Linear(hidden, hidden//2),
            torch.nn.ReLU())
        self.head_alpha = torch.nn.Linear(hidden//2, 1)
        self.head_delta = torch.nn.Linear(hidden//2, 1)

    def forward(self, hq, emb_x, feat_vec):
        x = torch.cat([self.ln_hq(hq), self.ln_emb(emb_x), feat_vec], dim=-1)
        h = self.fc(x)
        alpha_logit = self.head_alpha(h)
        delta = self.head_delta(h)
        return alpha_logit.squeeze(-1), delta.squeeze(-1)

class CandidateDataset(torch.utils.data.Dataset):
    def __init__(self, parquet_path):
        import pyarrow.parquet as pq
        import pandas as pd
        self.df = pq.read_table(parquet_path).to_pandas()
        # Build numeric arrays; normalize some features
        self.hq = np.stack(self.df['hq'].values).astype('float32')
        self.emb = np.stack(self.df['emb_x'].values).astype('float32')
        self.q_lp = self.df['q_logprob'].values.astype('float32')
        self.top2 = self.df['top2_margin'].values.astype('float32')
        self.Hq = self.df['Hq'].values.astype('float32')
        self.accept = self.df['accept'].values.astype('float32')
        self.delta = self.df['delta'].values.astype('float32')
        # Build decode-config one-hot
        # Assume columns: temperature, top_p, rep_pen, bans
        cfgs = []
        for r in self.df['decode_cfg']:
            # one-hot encoding example
            T = [1.0 if abs(r['temperature']-t)<1e-6 else 0.0 for t in [0.6,0.8,1.0,1.2]]
            P = [1.0 if abs(r['top_p']-p)<1e-6 else 0.0 for p in [0.8,0.9,0.95,1.0]]
            RP = [1.0 if abs(r['rep_pen']-rp)<1e-6 else 0.0 for rp in [1.0,1.1,1.2]]
            BL = [1.0 if (r['bans']!='none') else 0.0]
            cfgs.append(np.array(T+P+RP+BL, dtype='float32'))
        self.cfg = np.stack(cfgs)
        # Additional scalars packed into feat_vec
        self.feat = np.stack([self.q_lp, self.top2, self.Hq, np.zeros_like(self.q_lp), np.zeros_like(self.q_lp), np.zeros_like(self.q_lp)], axis=1).astype('float32')
        # Append cfg to feat in collate

    def __len__(self): return len(self.df)
    def __getitem__(self, i):
        feat = np.concatenate([self.feat[i], self.cfg[i]], axis=0)
        return self.hq[i], self.emb[i], feat, self.accept[i], self.delta[i]

# Training
from torch.utils.data import DataLoader, random_split
import torch, numpy as np

full = CandidateDataset('caves_candidates.parquet')
N = len(full)
train_N = int(0.8*N); val_N = N - train_N
train_ds, val_ds = random_split(full, [train_N, val_N], generator=torch.Generator().manual_seed(42))

def collate(batch):
    hq, emb, feat, acc, dlt = zip(*batch)
    return (torch.tensor(np.stack(hq)).cuda(),
            torch.tensor(np.stack(emb)).cuda(),
            torch.tensor(np.stack(feat)).cuda(),
            torch.tensor(np.array(acc)).cuda(),
            torch.tensor(np.array(dlt)).cuda())

train_dl = DataLoader(train_ds, batch_size=8192, shuffle=True, num_workers=4, collate_fn=collate, pin_memory=True)
val_dl = DataLoader(val_ds, batch_size=8192, shuffle=False, num_workers=2, collate_fn=collate)

model = AlphaEstimator(d_hq=full.hq.shape[1], d_emb=full.emb.shape[1], d_cfg=train_ds[0][2].shape[0])
model.cuda()
opt = torch.optim.AdamW(model.parameters(), lr=2e-4, weight_decay=0.01)

pos_weight = 2.0
bce = torch.nn.BCEWithLogitsLoss(pos_weight=torch.tensor(pos_weight).cuda())
huber = torch.nn.SmoothL1Loss()

for epoch in range(3):
    model.train()
    for hq, emb, feat, acc, dlt in train_dl:
        alpha_logit, dhat = model(hq, emb, feat)
        loss = bce(alpha_logit, acc) + 0.1*huber(dhat, dlt)
        opt.zero_grad(); loss.backward(); opt.step()
    # quick val
    model.eval(); tot=0; n=0
    with torch.no_grad():
        for hq, emb, feat, acc, dlt in val_dl:
            al, dh = model(hq, emb, feat)
            tot += torch.nn.functional.binary_cross_entropy_with_logits(al, acc).item()*acc.numel(); n += acc.numel()
    print('epoch', epoch, 'val_bce', tot/n)

Calibration: temperature scaling + isotonic regression + conformal LBs

# Gather val predictions
model.eval()
all_acc = []
all_logit = []
with torch.no_grad():
    for hq, emb, feat, acc, dlt in val_dl:
        al, _ = model(hq, emb, feat)
        all_acc.append(acc.cpu()); all_logit.append(al.cpu())
acc_t = torch.cat(all_acc).float().numpy()
logit_t = torch.cat(all_logit).float().numpy()

# Fit a scalar temperature T to minimize NLL on validation
log_T = torch.nn.Parameter(torch.tensor(0.0))
optT = torch.optim.LBFGS([log_T], lr=0.1, max_iter=100)
logits_tensor = torch.tensor(logit_t)
y_tensor = torch.tensor(acc_t)

def closure():
    optT.zero_grad()
    T = torch.exp(log_T)
    scaled = logits_tensor / T
    loss = torch.nn.functional.binary_cross_entropy_with_logits(scaled, y_tensor)
    loss.backward(); return loss
optT.step(closure)
T_hat = float(torch.exp(log_T).item())

# Isotonic regression on scaled probabilities
from sklearn.isotonic import IsotonicRegression
import numpy as np
p_scaled = 1.0/(1.0+np.exp(-logit_t/T_hat))
iso = IsotonicRegression(out_of_bounds='clip')
iso.fit(p_scaled, acc_t)

# Split-conformal one-sided lower bound
def conformal_lb(p_iso, y, delta=0.05):
    # Split calib set: use 50% of val
    n = len(y); idx = np.arange(n)
    np.random.seed(1337); np.random.shuffle(idx)
    calib = idx[: n//2]; test = idx[n//2:]
    r = p_iso[calib] - y[calib]
    q = np.quantile(r, 1.0-delta)
    return q, test

p_iso = iso.transform(p_scaled)
q_delta, test_idx = conformal_lb(p_iso, acc_t, delta=0.05)
a_phi_LB_val = np.clip(p_iso - q_delta, 0.0, 1.0)

# Store calibration artifacts for runtime
calibration = {'T': T_hat, 'iso_x': p_scaled, 'iso_y': acc_t, 'q_delta': float(q_delta)}

Evaluation A: calibration and generalization metrics
- Compute AUC and APS for the α-head; evaluate MAE for Δ.
- One-sided coverage: estimate Pr[accept ≤ aφ_LB + ε] ≥ 1−δ at ε≈0. Operationally, check that among candidates where aφ_LB ≥ α*, the empirical acceptance probability is ≥ α* in at least 95% of buckets and the global violation rate ≤ 5%.

Example evaluation code

from sklearn.metrics import roc_auc_score, average_precision_score
auc = roc_auc_score(acc_t[test_idx], 1/(1+np.exp(-logit_t[test_idx]/T_hat)))
aps = average_precision_score(acc_t[test_idx], 1/(1+np.exp(-logit_t[test_idx]/T_hat)))
mae_delta = np.mean(np.abs(full.df['delta'].values[test_idx] - 0.0))  # replace with predicted delta on val

# Coverage at alpha*=0.8 example
alpha_star = 0.8
mask = a_phi_LB_val[test_idx] >= alpha_star
emp_rate = acc_t[test_idx][mask].mean() if mask.any() else 0.0
print('AUC', auc, 'APS', aps, 'empirical acceptance under LB>=alpha*', emp_rate)

Evaluation B: offline drafting effectiveness
- Build a shadow simulator that, at each step, uses Mq to generate γ×B candidates, scores them with S′ ∝ aφ_LB · q(x) (rψ=0 for now), constructs the path maximizing product of aφ_LB across depth under node budget N, and then verifies proposals with Mp sequentially until rejection.
- Compare against baselines: uniform over q, top-q only, Δ̂-only.

Drafting simulation code (simplified; uses current aφ calibration)

class AphiRuntime:
    def __init__(self, model_path):
        self.model = AlphaEstimator(...).cuda().eval()
        # load weights; load calibration T_hat, iso, q_delta
        self.T = T_hat; self.iso = iso; self.qdelta = q_delta
    @torch.no_grad()
    def score(self, hq, emb, feat):
        alogit, _ = self.model(hq, emb, feat)
        p = torch.sigmoid(alogit / self.T).cpu().numpy()
        p_iso = self.iso.transform(p)
        lb = np.clip(p_iso - self.qdelta, 0.0, 1.0)
        return lb

@torch.no_grad()
def simulate_step(mp, mq, aphi, ids_mp, ids_mq, gamma=3, B=2, T=0.9, P=0.9):
    device = ids_mp.device
    # Propose tree
    nodes = [(ids_mq, [], 1.0)]  # (ids, path, prod_lb)
    all_candidates = []
    for depth in range(gamma):
        next_nodes = []
        for ids, path, prod in nodes:
            out = mq(input_ids=ids, output_hidden_states=True)
            logits_q = out.logits[:, -1, :].float()
            probs_q = torch.softmax(logits_q / T, dim=-1)
            topk = torch.topk(probs_q, k=B)
            for k in range(B):
                tok = topk.indices[0, k]
                qlp = torch.log(probs_q[0, tok])
                hq = out.hidden_states[-1][:, -1, :]
                emb = mq.get_input_embeddings()(tok)
                # Build feature vector (ensure same normalization as training)
                sorted_lp, _ = torch.sort(torch.log_softmax(logits_q, dim=-1), descending=True)
                top2_margin = (sorted_lp[0, 0] - sorted_lp[0, 1]).item()
                Hq = -(probs_q * torch.log(probs_q + 1e-9)).sum().item()
                feat = torch.tensor([[float(qlp), float(top2_margin), float(Hq), 0,0,0] + [0]* (aphi.model.fc[0].in_features - hq.shape[-1]-mq.get_input_embeddings().embedding_dim - 6)], device=device)
                lb = aphi.score(hq.float(), emb.float().view(1,-1), feat.float()).item()
                score = lb * float(torch.exp(qlp))
                all_candidates.append((path + [int(tok)], prod*lb, score))
                next_ids = torch.cat([ids, tok.view(1,1).to(device)], dim=-1)
                next_nodes.append((next_ids, path + [int(tok)], prod*lb))
        # beam keep top N nodes by product of LBs
        next_nodes.sort(key=lambda x: x[2], reverse=True)
        nodes = next_nodes[: B]  # or a node budget rule
    # Choose best path
    nodes.sort(key=lambda x: x[2], reverse=True)
    best_path = nodes[0][1]
    # Verify sequentially with Mp
    accepted = []
    ids = ids_mp
    for t in best_path:
        logits_p = mp(input_ids=ids).logits[:, -1, :].float()
        tok_p = torch.multinomial(torch.softmax(logits_p / T, dim=-1), num_samples=1).item()
        if tok_p == t:
            accepted.append(t)
            ids = torch.cat([ids, torch.tensor([[t]], device=device)], dim=-1)
        else:
            break
    return accepted

Success criteria
- One-sided coverage ≥ 0.95 across regimes; AUC ≥ 0.80; at least 30% reduction in overestimation vs heuristics.
- +15–30% accepted-prefix length at fixed α relative to baselines; ≥2× reduction in LB-miss vs uncalibrated.

Ablations
- Remove Δ head; remove decode-config embedding; train only at single temperature vs mixed; add rψ trained to predict Mp logprob as a tiny 2-layer MLP and show marginal gains.

Reliability enhancements
- Use class-weighted BCE and early stopping on coverage; calibrate per-decode-config slices and aggregate conformal quantiles via Mondrian conformal if coverage varies across configs.


Experiment 2 — Cascaded block verification with candidate-only logits and early-exit margin head
Purpose
- Demonstrate that a cheap partial Mp (Stage A) with candidate-only logits and a margin predictor prunes unpromising branches, reducing full Mp compute while preserving exactness and α.

Design
- Partition Mp into layers 0..L′ and L′+1..L. Run 0..L′ for all frontier nodes to obtain h_{L′} and partial KVs. Compute candidate-only logits for the union of proposed tokens C with a gathered lm_head. Predict a confidence margin with gθ(h_{L′}); prune node-token pairs with small margin and/or aφ_LB below α*. Survivors proceed to full Mp (Stage B), which performs vanilla speculative acceptance and sampling.

Training early-exit head gθ
- Data: For 5K prompts, run Mp full forward at each step to collect h_{L′} (output_hidden_states=True) and final-step logits. Define m* = logit(top1) − logit(top2) at the final layer. Label accept=1 if the top1 token sampled under decode config equals the proposed token for that node.
- Train gθ: a small MLP that maps h_{L′} to predicted margin m̂. Loss: Huber. Calibrate θ_prune to ensure P(prune | accept) ≤ 1% on validation (99% recall on accepts). Optionally fit a per-config θ_prune table.

Code: partial forward and candidate-only logits

class PartialMp(torch.nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, mp):
        super().__init__(); self.mp = mp
        self.blocks = mp.model.layers  # llama-like
        self.embed_tokens = mp.model.embed_tokens
        self.norm = mp.model.norm
        self.lm_head = mp.lm_head

    @torch.no_grad()
    def forward_to(self, input_ids, past_key_values=None, stop_layer=8):
        # Returns h_{L′} for last position and kvs up to L′
        x = self.embed_tokens(input_ids)
        new_past = []
        for i, blk in enumerate(self.blocks):
            x, kv = blk(x, use_cache=True, past_key_value=None if past_key_values is None else past_key_values[i])
            new_past.append(kv)
            if i+1 == stop_layer:
                break
        x = self.norm(x)
        h_last = x[:, -1, :]  # [B, H]
        return h_last, new_past

@torch.no_grad()
def candidate_only_logits(h_last, lm_head_weight, token_ids):
    # lm_head_weight: [vocab, hidden]; token_ids: [K]
    W_sel = torch.index_select(lm_head_weight, 0, token_ids)  # [K, H]
    logits = torch.matmul(h_last, W_sel.t())  # [B, K]
    return logits

class MarginHead(torch.nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, hidden, inner=1024):
        super().__init__()
        self.net = torch.nn.Sequential(
            torch.nn.LayerNorm(hidden),
            torch.nn.Linear(hidden, inner), torch.nn.ReLU(),
            torch.nn.Linear(inner, 1))
    def forward(self, h_last): return self.net(h_last).squeeze(-1)

# Training margin head
@torch.no_grad()
def build_margin_dataset(mp, prompts, Lp=8, T=0.9, P=0.9):
    hs, margins = [], []
    tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(...)
    for pr in prompts:
        ids = tok(pr, return_tensors='pt').to('cuda')
        out = mp(**ids, output_hidden_states=True)
        hL = out.hidden_states[Lp][:, -1, :].float()  # depends on model exposing
        logits = out.logits[:, -1, :].float()
        top2 = torch.topk(logits, k=2, dim=-1).values
        mstar = (top2[...,0]-top2[...,1]).cpu().numpy()
        hs.append(hL.cpu().numpy()); margins.append(mstar)
    return torch.tensor(np.concatenate(hs)), torch.tensor(np.concatenate(margins))

# Fit and choose theta to preserve 99% of acceptances

Decode-time pipeline
- For each frontier node:
  1) Stage A: run PartialMp.forward_to(ids, stop_layer=L′) to get h_{L′} and partial KVs.
  2) Build union C of candidate tokens across frontier. Compute candidate-only logits for all nodes with candidate_only_logits(h_last, W, C). Optionally, apply decode config temperature/top-p to these logits to estimate p(x) quickly; do not finalize acceptance here.
  3) Compute gθ(h_{L′}) per node. Combine with aφ_LB for each node-token to compute a conservative prune score. Prune pairs where gθ margin < θ_prune or aφ_LB < α*, but keep at least one child per node.
  4) Stage B: For survivors only, run mp forward from L′+1..L, either by resuming with cached KVs (if model API allows) or recomputing layers 0..L′ for survivors. Perform standard speculative acceptance.

Exactness checks
- Ensure pruning only reduces which candidates are verified; final acceptance sampling uses Mp identically to baseline. With fixed RNG seeds, generated outputs should match Baseline-0 ≥ 99% of runs. Any mismatch indicates a bug in acceptance or sampling, not pruning.

Metrics and measurement
- Tokens/sec end-to-end; Mp flops/token proxy: (n_full·L + n_partial·L′)/tokens.
- Fraction pruned; precision/recall of pruning for rejects; α mean/P95 unchanged vs Baseline-0.
- GPU timing: torch.cuda.Event timers around Stage A and B. Memory traffic proxy via torch.profiler.

Success criteria
- ≥15% reduction in Stage B full-layer tokens processed; ≥10% wall-clock speedup at γ∈{3,4}, B∈{2,4} vs Baseline-0; α unchanged; output equality ≥99% with fixed seeds.

Implementation notes
- KV reuse in HF: not directly exposed for mid-layer resume; acceptable to recompute 0..L′ in prototype. For production, custom forward can preserve KVs and resume.
- Candidate-only logits are bandwidth-light: gather K tokens across frontier; typical K ≪ vocab.
- Optional: 8-bit quantize Stage A blocks with bitsandbytes (bnb.nn.Linear8bitLt) to reduce time.


Experiment 3 — α-SLA constrained controller under mixed decode configs
Purpose
- Show that a dual controller maintains α ≥ α* per request with low violation rate across heterogeneous decode configs and increases throughput vs static settings.

Design
- Use aφ_LB from Experiment 1 and optionally Stage A from Experiment 2. Controller operates per request and step, updating a dual variable λA based on EMA(αobs). Actuators: tree depth γ, branching B, Mq temperature Tq, and an optional Stage-A prune threshold scale. Draft selection uses S′ ∝ aφ_LB · q(x) with a penalty on candidates where aφ_LB < α*.

Controller algorithm
- State: EMA α̂ with β=0.9; λA initialized 0.
- Update: λA ← clip(λA + η(α* − α̂), [0, λmax]) with η ∈ {0.05, 0.1}.
- Allocation: Node budget N ∈ [Nmin, Nmax] is a decreasing function of λA and uncertainty u (conformal interval width). Example: N = round(Nmax · sigmoid(−k·λA) · (1−u)), clipped to [Nmin, Nmax]. Uncertainty u estimated as mean max(0, p_iso − aφ_LB) across candidates.
- Actuators: map N to (γ,B) via a small table favoring deeper paths when aφ_LB high; adjust Tq ∈ [0.7,1.0] to nudge q→p when α dips (decrease Tq when α̂ < α*).
- Safety: If running EMA below α* for M consecutive steps or uncertainty high, fallback to baseline speculative (γ=2,B=1,Tq=0.9).

Code skeleton

class AlphaController:
    def __init__(self, alpha_star=0.8, eta=0.1, lam_max=5.0, beta=0.9, Nmin=2, Nmax=12):
        self.alpha_star = alpha_star; self.eta = eta; self.lam_max = lam_max
        self.beta = beta; self.Nmin = Nmin; self.Nmax = Nmax
        self.reset()
    def reset(self):
        self.alpha_hat = 1.0; self.lam = 0.0
    def update(self, accepts):
        # accepts: list of 0/1 for proposals verified this step
        a = np.mean(accepts) if len(accepts)>0 else 1.0
        self.alpha_hat = self.beta*self.alpha_hat + (1-self.beta)*a
        self.lam = np.clip(self.lam + self.eta*(self.alpha_star - self.alpha_hat), 0.0, self.lam_max)
    def choose(self, unc):
        # unc in [0,1]
        k = 1.2
        frac = 1/(1+np.exp(k*self.lam)) * (1-unc)
        N = int(np.clip(round(self.Nmax*frac), self.Nmin, self.Nmax))
        # map N to (gamma,B)
        if N <= 3: gamma,B = 2,1
        elif N <= 6: gamma,B = 3,2
        elif N <= 9: gamma,B = 4,2
        else: gamma,B = 5,2
        # Tq: cooler if alpha low
        Tq = float(np.clip(0.7 + 0.3*(self.alpha_hat/self.alpha_star), 0.7, 1.0))
        return gamma, B, Tq

@torch.no_grad()
def run_request(mp, mq, aphi, controller, prompt, cfg_sampler, use_stageA=False):
    # Returns per-step logs including alpha, throughput proxies
    logs = []
    mp_tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(...)
    mq_tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(...)
    ids_mp = mp_tok(prompt, return_tensors='pt').to('cuda')
    ids_mq = mq_tok(prompt, return_tensors='pt').to('cuda')
    controller.reset()
    step = 0
    while step < 128:
        gamma,B,Tq = controller.choose(unc=0.0)
        # Propose candidates and score
        candidates = []
        ids = ids_mq['input_ids']
        for d in range(gamma):
            out = mq(input_ids=ids, output_hidden_states=True)
            probs_q = torch.softmax(out.logits[:, -1, :]/Tq, dim=-1)
            topk = torch.topk(probs_q, k=B)
            for k in range(B):
                tok = topk.indices[0,k]
                hq = out.hidden_states[-1][:, -1, :]
                emb = mq.get_input_embeddings()(tok)
                feat = ...  # as in Exp1
                lb = aphi.score(hq.float(), emb.float().view(1,-1), feat.float()).item()
                candidates.append({'tok':int(tok), 'lb':lb, 'q':float(probs_q[0,tok])})
            ids = torch.cat([ids, topk.indices[:,0:1]], dim=-1)  # follow best for depth growth
        # Penalty for lb below alpha*
        for c in candidates:
            c['S'] = c['lb'] * c['q'] * np.exp(-max(0.0, controller.alpha_star - c['lb']) * controller.lam)
        candidates.sort(key=lambda x: x['S'], reverse=True)
        # Verify with Mp sequentially along best path
        accepts = []
        ids_cur = ids_mp['input_ids']
        for c in candidates[:gamma]:
            logits = mp(input_ids=ids_cur).logits[:, -1, :]
            sampled = torch.multinomial(torch.softmax(logits, dim=-1), num_samples=1).item()
            accept = int(sampled == c['tok'])
            accepts.append(accept)
            if accept:
                ids_cur = torch.cat([ids_cur, torch.tensor([[c['tok']]], device=ids_cur.device)], dim=-1)
            else:
                break
        ids_mp['input_ids'] = ids_cur; ids_mq['input_ids'] = ids_cur
        controller.update(accepts)
        logs.append({'accepts': accepts, 'alpha_hat': controller.alpha_hat, 'lambda': controller.lam})
        step += 1
    return logs

Protocol and baselines
- 3K requests; per request sample a decode-config from Exp1 distribution. Arms:
  1) Static: γ=3, B=2, Tq=0.9.
  2) Heuristic: if αhat < α* then decrease Tq by 0.05, else increase; clamp γ,B fixed.
  3) CAVES controller: full algorithm above.
- For reproducibility, fix random seeds and re-use the same prompt-config assignment across arms.

Metrics
- SLA: violation rate Pr[rolling α (window=16) < α*]; report per-request and global; P50/P95 α.
- Throughput: tokens/sec (median and P95 tail), Mp-calls/token, accepted-prefix length.
- Stability: variance of λA and frequency of fallback to baseline; overhead: % time in aφ and control logic via timers.

Success criteria
- SLA: violation rate ≤ 0.05; P95 α ≥ α* − 0.02.
- Throughput: ≥10–25% tokens/sec improvement vs Static at same α*; ≥2× reduction in P95 tail-latency variability.
- Overhead: aφ + control < 8% wall time.


Cross-experiment integration and non-overlap
- Experiment 1 focuses on calibrating aφ and demonstrating drafting gains without Stage A or control. Its calibrated model is consumed by Experiments 2 and 3.
- Experiment 2 isolates the impact of Stage A pruning on compute and exactness, holding drafting policy constant (can use aφ_LB thresholds but not the full controller).
- Experiment 3 evaluates the closed-loop controller using aφ_LB (and optionally Stage A) to enforce α SLAs under mixed decode configs. It measures stability and throughput benefits beyond Exp1/Exp2.

Reliability and safeguards
- Exactness preservation: In all experiments, final acceptance uses Mp’s standard speculative sampling. Stage A only decides which branches proceed to full verification; pruning reduces accepted-prefix opportunities but cannot alter Mp’s distribution on the output tokens.
- Calibration robustness: Use split-conformal LBs with Mondrian grouping over decode-config bins to maintain one-sided coverage across regimes. Penalize overestimation via asymmetric BCE (pos_weight>1) and check coverage per-bin.
- Uncertainty gating: Downweight or cap expansion when conformal intervals are wide (p_iso − LB large). This is realized in Experiment 3’s node-budget allocator.
- Reproducibility: Fix seeds, set deterministic flags, log all decode-configs, controller states, and random draws for acceptance checks; for exactness tests, ensure identical outputs vs Baseline-0 on fixed seeds.

Measurement and analysis utilities
- Use sklearn metrics (roc_auc_score, average_precision_score) for α-head; calibration curves and reliability diagrams from sklearn.calibration if desired.
- Coverage evaluation: bucket predictions by LB thresholds and compute empirical accept rates; report global and per-config coverage.
- Timing with torch.cuda.Event for Stage A/B; end-to-end tokens/sec by wall clock.
- Logging format: JSONL per request-step including accepts, α̂, λA, actuators (γ,B,Tq), uncertainty, and timing; aggregate with pandas.

Expected outcomes and interpretation
- Experiment 1: aφ achieves ≥0.95 one-sided coverage and provides +15–30% accepted-prefix length in shadow drafting at fixed α, validating the acceptance-aware drafting principle.
- Experiment 2: Stage A prunes ≥30–50% of node-token pairs with negligible false-prune on true accepts, reducing full-layer compute by ≥15% and improving wall time by ≥10% without changing α or outputs.
- Experiment 3: The controller maintains α≥α* with ≤5% violation rate, improves median tokens/sec by ≥10–25% vs static, and stabilizes tail latency (≥2× reduction in P95 variability), demonstrating SLA-oriented decode-time control.

Notes on practicality and extensions
- Micro-model sizes: keep aφ and rψ <10M parameters. Share an encoder (e.g., a tiny 1D Transformer over concatenated features) if CPU-GPU transfers dominate; keep all inference on GPU.
- Quantization: Apply 8-bit linear to Stage A blocks; optionally 4-bit GPTQ on Mq to save memory; these do not affect correctness.
- MoE support: Stage A can gate experts based on candidate-only logits and carry masks to Stage B; omitted in prototype but compatible.
- Candidate-only logits kernel: For production, implement fused gather–matmul to reduce launches; prototype uses torch.index_select.
- Safety fallback: Persistent α SLA violations trigger a switch to baseline speculative decoding; log and alarm for recalibration of aφ.

import os
import math
import json
import time
import random
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import List, Tuple, Dict, Any

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F
from torch.utils.data import Dataset, DataLoader
from sklearn.isotonic import IsotonicRegression
from sklearn.metrics import roc_auc_score, average_precision_score
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
from tqdm import tqdm

# -------------------------------
# Global Settings and Utilities
# -------------------------------

def set_seed(seed: int = 1337):
    random.seed(seed)
    np.random.seed(seed)
    torch.manual_seed(seed)
    torch.cuda.manual_seed_all(seed)
    torch.backends.cudnn.deterministic = True
    try:
        torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True)
    except Exception:
        pass

DEVICE = torch.device('cuda' if torch.cuda.is_available() else 'cpu')

# -------------------------------
# Tiny Transformer Language Model
# -------------------------------

class TinyTransformerBlock(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, d_model: int, n_heads: int, d_ff: int, dropout: float = 0.0):
        super().__init__()
        self.attn = nn.MultiheadAttention(d_model, n_heads, dropout=dropout, batch_first=True)
        self.ln1 = nn.LayerNorm(d_model)
        self.ff = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(d_model, d_ff),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(d_ff, d_model)
        )
        self.ln2 = nn.LayerNorm(d_model)
        self.dropout = nn.Dropout(dropout)

    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor, attn_mask: torch.Tensor = None):
        # x: [B, T, H]
        attn_out, _ = self.attn(x, x, x, attn_mask=attn_mask, need_weights=False)
        x = self.ln1(x + self.dropout(attn_out))
        ff_out = self.ff(x)
        x = self.ln2(x + self.dropout(ff_out))
        return x

class TinyLM(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, vocab_size: int = 256, d_model: int = 64, n_layers: int = 6, n_heads: int = 4, d_ff: int = 128, max_seq_len: int = 512, dropout: float = 0.0):
        super().__init__()
        self.vocab_size = vocab_size
        self.d_model = d_model
        self.token_embed = nn.Embedding(vocab_size, d_model)
        self.pos_embed = nn.Embedding(max_seq_len, d_model)
        self.blocks = nn.ModuleList([TinyTransformerBlock(d_model, n_heads, d_ff, dropout) for _ in range(n_layers)])
        self.ln_f = nn.LayerNorm(d_model)
        self.lm_head = nn.Linear(d_model, vocab_size, bias=False)
        self.n_layers = n_layers
        self.max_seq_len = max_seq_len

        self.apply(self._init_weights)

    def _init_weights(self, module):
        if isinstance(module, nn.Linear):
            nn.init.xavier_uniform_(module.weight)
            if module.bias is not None:
                nn.init.zeros_(module.bias)
        elif isinstance(module, nn.Embedding):
            nn.init.normal_(module.weight, mean=0.0, std=0.02)

    def causal_mask(self, T: int):
        # [T, T] upper triangular mask with -inf above diagonal
        mask = torch.full((T, T), float('-inf'), device=DEVICE)
        mask = torch.triu(mask, diagonal=1)
        return mask

    def forward(self, input_ids: torch.Tensor, output_hidden_states: bool = False) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        B, T = input_ids.shape
        pos = torch.arange(T, device=input_ids.device).unsqueeze(0)
        x = self.token_embed(input_ids) + self.pos_embed(pos)
        attn_mask = self.causal_mask(T)
        hidden_states = []
        for i, blk in enumerate(self.blocks):
            x = blk(x, attn_mask)
            if output_hidden_states:
                hidden_states.append(x.clone())
        x = self.ln_f(x)
        logits = self.lm_head(x)
        out = {'logits': logits}
        if output_hidden_states:
            out['hidden_states'] = hidden_states  # list length n_layers, each [B,T,H]
        return out

    @torch.no_grad()
    def forward_to(self, input_ids: torch.Tensor, stop_layer: int = 2) -> Tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
        # Returns h_{L'} for last position and hidden states up to L'
        B, T = input_ids.shape
        pos = torch.arange(T, device=input_ids.device).unsqueeze(0)
        x = self.token_embed(input_ids) + self.pos_embed(pos)
        attn_mask = self.causal_mask(T)
        for i, blk in enumerate(self.blocks):
            x = blk(x, attn_mask)
            if (i + 1) == stop_layer:
                break
        x = self.ln_f(x)
        h_last = x[:, -1, :]  # [B, H]
        return h_last, x  # return full partial output if needed

    @torch.no_grad()
    def candidate_only_logits(self, h_last: torch.Tensor, token_ids: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        # h_last: [B,H]; token_ids: [K]
        W = self.lm_head.weight  # [V, H]
        W_sel = torch.index_select(W, dim=0, index=token_ids)
        logits = h_last @ W_sel.t()  # [B,K]
        return logits

# -------------------------------
# Sampling Utilities
# -------------------------------

def apply_repetition_penalty(logits: torch.Tensor, prev_tokens: torch.Tensor, penalty: float):
    if penalty == 1.0:
        return logits
    # simple repetition penalty: divide logits of prev tokens by penalty (increase negative)
    for t in prev_tokens.tolist():
        logits[..., t] /= penalty
    return logits

@torch.no_grad()
def top_p_filtering(logits: torch.Tensor, top_p: float = 1.0):
    if top_p >= 1.0:
        return logits
    sorted_logits, sorted_indices = torch.sort(logits, descending=True)
    cumprobs = torch.cumsum(F.softmax(sorted_logits, dim=-1), dim=-1)
    mask = cumprobs > top_p
    mask[..., 0] = False
    sorted_logits[mask] = float('-inf')
    logits[0, sorted_indices[0]] = sorted_logits[0]
    return logits

@torch.no_grad()
def sample_next_token(logits: torch.Tensor, temperature: float = 1.0, top_p: float = 1.0):
    logits = logits / max(temperature, 1e-6)
    logits = top_p_filtering(logits, top_p)
    probs = F.softmax(logits, dim=-1)
    tok = torch.multinomial(probs, num_samples=1)
    return tok.squeeze(-1)

# -------------------------------
# Synthetic Data Generator
# -------------------------------

@dataclass
class DecodeConfig:
    temperature: float
    top_p: float
    rep_pen: float
    ban_flag: int  # 0/1

class SyntheticPromptGenerator:
    def __init__(self, vocab_size: int, domain: str, seq_len: int = 32):
        self.vocab_size = vocab_size
        self.seq_len = seq_len
        rng = np.random.default_rng(123 if domain == 'chat' else 321)
        # Domain-specific bigram distributions for diversity
        base = rng.random((vocab_size, vocab_size))
        for i in range(vocab_size):
            base[i] += (i % 7) * 0.05  # induce structure
        self.bigram = base / base.sum(axis=1, keepdims=True)
        self.start_probs = rng.random(vocab_size)
        self.start_probs /= self.start_probs.sum()

    def generate(self, n_prompts: int) -> List[List[int]]:
        prompts = []
        for _ in range(n_prompts):
            seq = [int(np.random.choice(self.vocab_size, p=self.start_probs))]
            for _ in range(self.seq_len - 1):
                prev = seq[-1]
                seq.append(int(np.random.choice(self.vocab_size, p=self.bigram[prev])))
            prompts.append(seq)
        return prompts

# -------------------------------
# Candidate Logging (Baseline Speculative Decoding)
# -------------------------------

@dataclass
class SpecConfig:
    gamma: int = 2
    B: int = 2
    max_new_tokens: int = 32

class SpecLogger:
    def __init__(self, mp: TinyLM, mq: TinyLM, vocab_size: int, ban_list: List[int]):
        self.mp = mp
        self.mq = mq
        self.vocab_size = vocab_size
        self.ban_list = set(ban_list)

    @torch.no_grad()
    def collect(self, prompts: List[List[int]], spec: SpecConfig,
                cfg_sampler, n_steps: int = 24) -> pd.DataFrame:
        rows = []
        pid = 0
        for prompt in tqdm(prompts, desc='Collecting candidates'):
            # Initialize contexts for Mp and Mq
            ids_mp = torch.tensor([prompt], device=DEVICE, dtype=torch.long)
            ids_mq = torch.tensor([prompt], device=DEVICE, dtype=torch.long)
            accepted_hist = []
            step_id = 0
            while step_id < n_steps:
                cfg: DecodeConfig = cfg_sampler()
                T, P, rep_pen, ban_flag = cfg.temperature, cfg.top_p, cfg.rep_pen, cfg.ban_flag
                # Propose draft tree with Mq
                frontier = [(ids_mq.clone(), [])]
                proposals = []  # per-candidate rows
                for depth in range(spec.gamma):
                    new_frontier = []
                    for ids, path in frontier:
                        out_q = self.mq(ids, output_hidden_states=True)
                        logits_q = out_q['logits'][:, -1, :]
                        logits_q = apply_repetition_penalty(logits_q.clone(), ids[0], rep_pen)
                        probs_q = F.softmax(logits_q / max(T, 1e-6), dim=-1)
                        topk = torch.topk(probs_q, k=spec.B)
                        sorted_lp, sorted_idx = torch.sort(torch.log_softmax(logits_q, dim=-1), descending=True)
                        top2_margin = float((sorted_lp[0, 0] - sorted_lp[0, 1]).item())
                        Hq = float((-(probs_q * torch.log(probs_q + 1e-9)).sum()).item())
                        hq = out_q['hidden_states'][-1][:, -1, :].detach()  # [1,H]
                        for k in range(spec.B):
                            tok = int(topk.indices[0, k].item())
                            # Ban handling: if ban_flag and tok in ban list, mark
                            ban_hit = 1 if (ban_flag == 1 and tok in self.ban_list) else 0
                            qlp = float(torch.log(probs_q[0, tok] + 1e-9).item())
                            emb_x = self.mq.token_embed.weight[tok].detach().cpu().numpy()
                            # Collect proposal features
                            proposals.append({
                                'prompt_id': pid,
                                'step_id': step_id,
                                'tok': tok,
                                'q_logprob': qlp,
                                'top2_margin': top2_margin,
                                'Hq': Hq,
                                'hq': hq[0].detach().cpu().numpy(),
                                'emb_x': emb_x,
                                'temperature': T,
                                'top_p': P,
                                'rep_pen': rep_pen,
                                'ban_flag': ban_flag,
                                'alpha_hist_mean': float(np.mean(accepted_hist[-4:]) if len(accepted_hist) else 1.0),
                                'dist_eos': float(spec.max_new_tokens - step_id),
                                'ban_hit': ban_hit,
                                'context_len': int(ids.shape[1]),
                            })
                            new_ids = torch.cat([ids, torch.tensor([[tok]], device=DEVICE)], dim=-1)
                            new_frontier.append((new_ids, path + [tok]))
                    frontier = new_frontier
                # Compute Mp acceptance and deltas for labels
                out_p = self.mp(ids_mp)
                logits_p = out_p['logits'][:, -1, :]
                logits_p = apply_repetition_penalty(logits_p.clone(), ids_mp[0], rep_pen)
                # Sample token under Mp
                sampled_tok = int(sample_next_token(logits_p, temperature=T, top_p=P)[0].item())
                p_lp = torch.log_softmax(logits_p / max(T, 1e-6), dim=-1)
                out_q_now = self.mq(ids_mq)
                q_lp_now = torch.log_softmax(out_q_now['logits'][:, -1, :] / max(T, 1e-6), dim=-1)
                for row in proposals:
                    t = row['tok']
                    delta = float((p_lp[0, t] - q_lp_now[0, t]).item())
                    accept = 1 if t == sampled_tok else 0
                    row.update({'delta': delta, 'accept': accept})
                # Advance contexts by Mp's actual sampled token
                ids_mp = torch.cat([ids_mp, torch.tensor([[sampled_tok]], device=DEVICE)], dim=-1)
                ids_mq = torch.cat([ids_mq, torch.tensor([[sampled_tok]], device=DEVICE)], dim=-1)
                accepted_hist.append(1)  # by definition we advanced with Mp sample
                rows.extend(proposals)
                step_id += 1
                if step_id >= spec.max_new_tokens:
                    break
            pid += 1
        df = pd.DataFrame(rows)
        return df

class AlphaEstimator(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, d_hq: int, d_emb: int, d_cfg: int = 13, hidden: int = 256):
        super().__init__()
        self.ln_hq = nn.LayerNorm(d_hq)
        self.ln_emb = nn.LayerNorm(d_emb)
        # feat_vec includes scalar features + decode-config one-hot
        self.fc = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(d_hq + d_emb + d_cfg, hidden),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Dropout(0.1),
            nn.Linear(hidden, hidden // 2),
            nn.ReLU(),
        )
        self.head_alpha = nn.Linear(hidden // 2, 1)
        self.head_delta = nn.Linear(hidden // 2, 1)

    def forward(self, hq: torch.Tensor, emb_x: torch.Tensor, feat_vec: torch.Tensor):
        x = torch.cat([self.ln_hq(hq), self.ln_emb(emb_x), feat_vec], dim=-1)
        h = self.fc(x)
        alpha_logit = self.head_alpha(h).squeeze(-1)
        delta = self.head_delta(h).squeeze(-1)
        return alpha_logit, delta

class CandidateTensorDataset(Dataset):
    def __init__(self, df: pd.DataFrame, vocab_size: int):
        self.df = df.reset_index(drop=True)
        # Extract arrays
        self.hq = np.stack(self.df['hq'].values).astype('float32')
        self.emb = np.stack(self.df['emb_x'].values).astype('float32')
        self.q_lp = self.df['q_logprob'].astype('float32').values
        self.top2 = self.df['top2_margin'].astype('float32').values
        self.Hq = self.df['Hq'].astype('float32').values
        self.acc = self.df['accept'].astype('float32').values
        self.delta = self.df['delta'].astype('float32').values
        self.alpha_hist_mean = self.df['alpha_hist_mean'].astype('float32').values
        self.dist_eos = self.df['dist_eos'].astype('float32').values
        self.ban_hit = self.df['ban_hit'].astype('float32').values
        # Decode-config one-hot: T in {0.6,0.8,1.0,1.2}, top_p in {0.8,0.9,0.95,1.0}, rep_pen in {1.0,1.1,1.2}, ban_flag {0,1}
        Ts = [0.6, 0.8, 1.0, 1.2]
        Ps = [0.8, 0.9, 0.95, 1.0]
        RPs = [1.0, 1.1, 1.2]
        cfg = []
        for i in range(len(self.df)):
            row = self.df.iloc[i]
            oneT = [1.0 if abs(row['temperature'] - t) < 1e-6 else 0.0 for t in Ts]
            oneP = [1.0 if abs(row['top_p'] - p) < 1e-6 else 0.0 for p in Ps]
            oneRP = [1.0 if abs(row['rep_pen'] - rp) < 1e-6 else 0.0 for rp in RPs]
            oneBAN = [1.0 if int(row['ban_flag']) == 1 else 0.0]
            cfg.append(np.array(oneT + oneP + oneRP + oneBAN, dtype='float32'))
        self.cfg = np.stack(cfg, axis=0)
        # Build final feat vector: [q_lp, top2, Hq, alpha_hist_mean, dist_eos_norm, ban_hit] + cfg
        dist_eos_norm = (self.dist_eos / (self.dist_eos.max() + 1e-6)).astype('float32')
        base = np.stack([self.q_lp, self.top2, self.Hq, self.alpha_hist_mean, dist_eos_norm, self.ban_hit], axis=1).astype('float32')
        self.feat = np.concatenate([base, self.cfg], axis=1).astype('float32')
        self.d_cfg = self.feat.shape[1] - self.hq.shape[1] - self.emb.shape[1]  # not used directly here

    def __len__(self):
        return len(self.df)

    def __getitem__(self, idx):
        return (
            torch.tensor(self.hq[idx], dtype=torch.float32),
            torch.tensor(self.emb[idx], dtype=torch.float32),
            torch.tensor(self.feat[idx], dtype=torch.float32),
            torch.tensor(self.acc[idx], dtype=torch.float32),
            torch.tensor(self.delta[idx], dtype=torch.float32),
        )

# Calibration utilities
